Caveats and open checks

  • DEV results are development evidence; the rule, budgets, box and arms were fixed after the stock-card RRMS and a 3-device box trial were seen and before any starting card on all DEV devices or any correction fit. TEST (24 devices) is not loaded.
  • The card is a generic 50-nm example card, not a card of the measured 40-nm process, with the temperature coefficients set to 0; it is not calibrated for either temperature. The stock-card RRMS is 0.66-23.1 per device and temperature; the starting cards come from a 43-parameter fit with a box of |v|/10..10|v|.
  • The 2-8 devices of one geometry are copies on one die and are not independent; the cluster-bootstrap CIs (7 groups) include 1 for R1 at both temperatures and for K. The rule uses the device bootstrap.
  • B1 returned the starting card unchanged for 16/45 devices at 4.13 K and 13/45 at 295.0 K and is above C0_refit on 34/45 and 33/45 devices.
  • The sweeps start near or above threshold (Vg from 0.45 / 0.30 V nMOS, -0.60 / -0.40 V pMOS); there is no deep-subthreshold data.
  • Training pools hold 31-43 devices of both polarities (sky130 I3-2: 11 devices; IHP I5-1: 7 or 9 within class).
  • The M_bias I-V curves are ngspice-41 currents of the refit card multiplied by exp(g) in Python, not SPICE-native simulations of the correction.

Claim i6-1 · updated 2026-10-20

refutedI5-1: on 18 IHP SG13G2 measured DEV DUTs (PSP103, NGSpice-46) at 300 K, the I3-2 correction M_bias with the recipe unchanged gives a higher held-out RRMS than the no-correction refit C0_refit (GMR(M_bias, C0_refit) 1.214 [1.008, 1.537], 9/18 DUTs lower); the pre-registered rule output is 'not replicated' (R1 fails), and the baseline rule output is 'matched by B1, B2'. 233, 343 and 398 K (secondary) are also not replicated. DEV values are development evidence.not replicated on IHP SG13G2 room-temperature data 300 K, 18 IHP SG13G2 measured DEV DUTs, leave-one-DUT-out within class, strict paper RRMS (inclusion frozen from the measured current) after the held-out 12-parameter PSP card refit; R1 needs the device-bootstrap 95% CI upper bound of GMR(M_bias, C0_refit) < 1: 1.214 [1.008, 1.537]

What it is

Question: does the I3-2 result (M_bias in the held-out card refit gives lower held-out RRMS than the refit without it, and is not worse than T1 + 0.005) hold on a second, independent set of measured devices from a different process and compact model?

  • Data: IHP-Open-PDK ihp-sg13g2/libs.doc/meas/MOS (commit 5e6d592e, Apache-2.0): 28 DUTs (LV 8 nMOS + 8 pMOS, HV 6 + 6), 233/300/343/398 K; the 11 Vb = 0 curves per DUT and temperature; 946 of 1232 curves included by the measured-current rule. Split DEV 18 / TEST 10 (seed 20261020); TEST not loaded.
  • Cards: stock PSP103 PDK card; 12-parameter pdk2 IHP wide set fitted from the stock card (starting card); every held-out arm refits from the starting card (max_nfev 400, irls 2).
  • Arms: C0_refit (control), M_bias (I3-2 recipe unchanged; training within class, VDD 1.2 V LV / 3.3 V HV), T1_inloop, B1 (wider PSP set), B2 (extrinsic resistance + heating factor), B3_d3 (polynomial g), B5 (in-sample reference), X300 (300 K correction applied at 233/343/398 K).
  • Rule at 300 K: R1 CI upper of GMR(M_bias, C0_refit) < 1; R2 M_bias mean <= T1_inloop mean + 0.005; R3 0 failed -> 'replicated'. Baselines B1, B2, B3_d3 beaten if CI upper of GMR(M_bias, X) < 1.

What we did

  • Pre-registration out/research/explore/I5_1/prereg.json (commit 9267a90), committed before any card fit on the IHP data; the stock-card RRMS was seen before the rule was fixed.

  • Report scripts/research/plot_explore_i5_1.py (batch 2026-10-20_i5_1) recomputes every aggregate, paired ratio, per-class ratio, X300 ratio and the rule output from the stored per-DUT values and checks them against the stored values.

Caveats and open checks

  • DEV results are development evidence; the rule, budgets, box and arms were fixed after the stock-card RRMS was seen and before any fit. TEST (10 DUTs) is not loaded.

Claim i5-1 · updated 2026-10-20

refutedI3-1 (simulated devices): the hybrid temperature law hyb (per-device par3 law plus a learned population-shared residual) has GMR 0.741 [0.610, 0.901] vs par3 on tier M, 1.739 [1.432, 2.132] on tier W and 1.224 [1.062, 1.422] on the new tier H; it is not lower than lrn_mean on tier M (1.119 [0.951, 1.312]); the pre-registered rule output is KILL.KILL: GMR(hyb, par3) M 0.741, W 1.739, H 1.224 36 simulated test devices per tier, setting O4, per-device held-out RRMS = mean over 110/190/260 K; GMR = exp(mean log((a + 0.01) / (b + 0.01))) with 95% bootstrap CI (4000 resamples); u0 check valid on all tiers

What it is

Question: does a hybrid temperature law x(T) = par3_d(T) + sigma_h NN(geometry, par3 anchor residuals, T), with the per-device par3 law fitted on the O4 anchors (77/150/225/300 K) and a network shared across a densely characterised simulated population, predict the seven-parameter card at 110/190/260 K with lower NGSpice RRMS than par3 and lrn_mean when the truth law is outside the par3 family (tiers M and H), and not worse than par3 by more than a margin when the truth is inside it (tier W)?

The design addresses three E3b findings: lrn did not differ from lrn_mean on tier M; lrn lost to par3 on tier W; tier M and W were seen before the design. Tier H (piecewise-linear law with a kink plus a 5 K freeze-out step on vth0 and u0) was written in the pre-registration and not simulated before the decision run.

  • hyb network output initialised to 0, output penalty 0.01 mean(NN^2), early stopping that can return the zero-correction state; 5 members, each keeps the better of input sets geo_t and geo_t_res (addendum, before any NGSpice run of the new arms).
  • hyb_mean = par3 + population-mean residual per device type and temperature (no network).
  • CONTINUE: M1 GMR(hyb, par3) <= 0.80 with CI upper < 1; M2 CI upper of GMR(hyb, lrn_mean) < 1; M3 GMR(hyb, pt_interp) < 1; W1 CI upper of GMR(hyb, par3) on W <= 1.25; H1 CI upper of GMR(hyb, par3) on H < 1; H2 GMR(hyb, lrn_mean) < 1 and GMR(hyb, pt_interp) < 1 on H; F failed cells <= 10%.
  • KILL: not CONTINUE and any of GMR(hyb, par3) >= 0.95 (M), >= 1.50 (W), >= 1.00 (H). INCONCLUSIVE otherwise.

What we did

  • Pre-registration out/research/explore/I3_1/prereg.json (commit c877413) and prereg_addendum.json (hyb inputs and output penalty); code commit c59ce14 (src/cryoml/explore/i3_hybrid.py, tier H generator in src/cryoml/explore/e3_temp.py, scripts/research/explore/e3_temp_misspec.py --study I3_1).
  • Queue jobs I3_1_full_M (2026-10-20 01:55-02:22, 1629 s; 144 training devices for the scaling arm, 72 primary), I3_1_full_W (02:22-02:40), I3_1_full_H (02:40-02:58), I3_1_decide (02:58). 12 REAL_DEV geometries, 36 simulated test devices per tier; no measured I-V.
  • Report scripts/research/plot_explore_i3_1_i3_2f.py (batch 2026-10-20_i3_1_i3_2f) recomputes every GMR, CI and win count from eval/*.json and checks them against decision.json, and re-evaluates the rule.

hyb applies the correction at the anchor temperatures as well; its anchor-temperature mean RRMS is 0.213 (M), 0.089 (W) and 0.178 (H), against 0.171, 0.038 and 0.081 for par3 and 0.015, 0.012 and 0.013 for lrn, which returns the anchor fits at the anchors.

On tier H, lrn (the E3b method) has GMR 0.752 [0.640, 0.886] vs par3 and 0.802 [0.697, 0.919] vs lrn_mean, and 1.083 [1.010, 1.164] vs pt_interp (lower on 15/36). Its E3-rule output on tier H is INCONCLUSIVE (R_O4 0.145 < 0.25; reduction vs pt_interp 0.049 < 0.10). On tier W lrn has GMR 2.603 vs par3 (E3-rule output INCONCLUSIVE, as in E3b).

Scaling (tier M): from 36 to 144 training devices the lrn held-out mean goes 0.2644 -> 0.2778 -> 0.2468 and hyb 0.3333 -> 0.3086 -> 0.3102.

No hyb ensemble member returned the zero-correction state (best steps M 75-2999, W 25-375, H 50-125). Existing arms reproduce the E3b full runs on tiers M and W (max |difference| 0; O2 par3_pop 1.7e-7 on M).

Caveats and open checks

  • Simulated devices only; training and test devices of each tier come from the same generator (no train-on-one-law, test-on-another condition).
  • Tier H was written by the same authors as tiers M and W, after seeing E3b; it is new to the hybrid design but not independent of the authors' assumptions about temperature laws.
  • The hyb inputs and output penalty were changed by the addendum after a synthetic unit test and before any NGSpice run of the new arms.
  • hyb has no gating at the anchor temperatures (pre-registered); its anchor-temperature error enters the card at all temperatures.

Device-venue candidate. Cold-start reruns of the paper pipeline, direct NGSpice fits and a simulated temperature benchmark.

Status as of 2026-10-17

Setup and reference cards

  • Simulator: a native arm64 build of the ngspice-41 release (~/cryo-ng41/arm64/bin/ngspice); the x86_64 conda-forge build no longer runs on macOS 27. It reproduces the reference scores exactly, and verify_simulator.py agrees with the upstream sweeps to ≤1e-11 A.

verifiedWith 43 parameters and a cold start, direct NGSpice reaches 0.1044 all-device after FD; the paper's 43-parameter card scores 0.2038.0.1044 vs 0.2038 all-device, after FD (combined 0.0976 vs 0.1905)

What it is

Question: how low can the measured-data RRMS go with 43 parameters when no released 77 K multiplier is used?

Direct NGSpice: CMA-ES then TRF directly on NGSpice (scripts/research/ngspice_direct.py), round 1 seeded from the seven-parameter fit, rounds 2 and 3 re-centred with the cold-loop rule. Paper pipeline: bank → surrogate → multistart surrogate FD → NGSpice validation, four rounds. FD: uniform polish for every method.

What we did

  • Direct NGSpice 43: full_r1_direct_seeded → full_r2_direct → full_r3_direct, about 21.9k NGSpice calls per device in round 1 (TRF Jacobians included); direct43_r3_fd polish (314 calls per device).
  • Pipeline 43: scripts/research/cold_loop.py --set full, rounds 1–4, finished 2026-10-16 05:39 (12.4 h); fd_pipe43_r4_real (338 s) polished the round-4 card selected before the fix and is superseded by fd_pipe43_r4_fixed (33 s, 2026-10-17 07:13) on the corrected card.
  • All re-scored independently with scripts/research/verify_direct.py and verify_cold_results.py.
  • Final selection rerun for round 4 (logged 2026-10-16 22:18): out/research/pipe_fixed/full_r4, with the round-4 surrogate (forward-model checksum identical to out/cold_loop/full/round_4/extract/forward_model.pt) and the same rule. Only nmos_L8_W1p6 changes: its selected card changes from an FD endpoint with 9 of 10 included curves failed (stored 0.0263) to another FD endpoint (0.0431). The other 17 devices keep the same card and score.

Caveats and open checks

  • Correction (logged 2026-10-16 22:18): the pipeline's final selection was rerun for rounds 1 and 4 with the same surrogates and the rule that rejects candidates with failed included curves (out/research/pipe_fixed/full_r1, out/research/pipe_fixed/full_r4). Rounds 2–3 were not rerun. The round-4 box comes from the round-3 pick made before the fix.
  • Values before the fix, pipeline 43 round 4, all-device, raw / + FD: stored 0.1513 / 0.1465; valid-only 0.1586 / 0.1539 over 17 devices; penalized 0.6500 / 0.6455; 1 failed device (nmos_L8_W1p6, 9 of 10 included curves) (out/research/audit/failed_curves.json).
  • Dropped-curve bug: metrics.device_rrms_new averaged only the finite included curves, so a device whose included metric curve failed to simulate was stored with the mean of its surviving curves (upstream rrmsCalc.py gives NaN for that device), while the FD polish scored the same start with the penalized objective (RRMS 10 per failed curve). This gave the FD-start mismatches 0.2035 vs 1.1832 (pipeline 43 round 1, nmos_L0p15_W1p6, 1 of 10 included curves failed) and 0.0263 vs 9.0026 (pipeline 43 round 4, nmos_L8_W1p6, 9 of 10 failed). Fix: cryoml.strict_score marks such devices as failed and every report gives the failed-device count, the mean over valid devices and the penalized mean next to the stored value (commit 15d1f3e); polish_cards.py scores its start with final_score and records failed included curves (8302a9d); metrics.device_rrms_new now returns NaN for a device with a non-finite or missing included curve and the pipeline's NGSpice validation sorts such candidates last (a0e1e97). Result files written before the fix keep their stored values; out/research/audit/failed_curves.json recomputes the three values for 227 runs, 16 of which have a failed device.
  • About 6 of 43 parameters per device sit at the box edge in the direct fits (mostly secondary parameters held to ×3: dwg, k3b, pdiblc2, xj, prwg, k2). A physicality check is pending before any card is presented.
  • Direct NGSpice 43-parameter fits used about 21.9k NGSpice calls per device per round (TRF Jacobian evaluations included), not 3.3k as first logged.
  • These runs used the real devices, which are TEST data under the ICML protocol defined later the same day.

Claim cryo-43 · updated 2026-10-17

verifiedWith seven parameters the measured-data RRMS stops near 0.164 all-device; a 3× longer direct search changes it by 0.0005.0.1643 all-device, pipeline 7 round 4 + FD (combined 0.1548)

What it is

Question: is the seven-parameter error on measured data an optimization failure or a model-form limit?

Test: the same methods on held-out simulated devices, where the true card scores 0. A method that inverts the simulator there but not the measurements is limited by the seven-parameter model form.

What we did

  • Cold seven-parameter pipeline rounds 1–4 and direct NGSpice in the round-1 box, 2026-10-15; scores re-checked with scripts/research/verify_cold_results.py (out/research/verify_seven_r4.json).
  • Uniform FD polish of every method on real and three simulated sets (scripts/research/polish_cards.py).

Claim cryo-seven-floor · updated 2026-10-16

verifiedEach cold-pipeline round lowers the 43-parameter all-device RRMS: 0.2382, 0.1965, 0.1716, 0.1522 over rounds 1–4, with 18 of 18 devices valid in each round (rounds 1 and 4 from the final selection rerun with failed-curve rejection, rounds 2 and 3 as stored).0.2382 → 0.1522 all-device, raw, pipeline 43, rounds 1–4 (combined 0.2289 → 0.1437); stored before the fix: 0.2375 → 0.1513

What it is

Each round re-centres every device's box on its selected NGSpice-validated card; interior coordinates halve their log width, edge coordinates keep it so the box moves outward. Each round draws a new 10k bank per device and trains a new surrogate from random initialization.

What we did

  • scripts/research/cold_loop.py --set seven and --set full, rounds 1–4; 43-parameter rounds finished 2026-10-16 05:39 after 12.4 h; 40,035 cumulative NGSpice calls per device by round 4.
  • Direct NGSpice chain full_r1_direct_seeded → full_r2_direct → full_r3_direct (each spec's source_run names the previous round).
  • Final selection rerun for round 1 (logged 2026-10-16 22:18): out/research/pipe_fixed/full_r1, with the round-1 surrogate (forward-model checksum identical to out/cold_loop/full/round_1/extract/forward_model.pt) and the rule that rejects candidates with failed included curves (commit a0e1e97). Only nmos_L0p15_W1p6 changes: its selected card changes from an FD endpoint (0.2035, 1 of 10 included curves failed) to a bank start (0.2159). The other 17 devices keep the same card and score.
  • Final selection rerun for round 4 (logged 2026-10-16 22:18): out/research/pipe_fixed/full_r4, with the round-4 surrogate (forward-model checksum identical to out/cold_loop/full/round_4/extract/forward_model.pt) and the same rule. Only nmos_L8_W1p6 changes: its selected card changes from an FD endpoint with 9 of 10 included curves failed (stored 0.0263) to another FD endpoint (0.0431). The other 17 devices keep the same card and score.

Fix: cryoml.strict_score marks such devices as failed and every report gives the failed-device count, the mean over valid devices and the penalized mean next to the stored value (commit 15d1f3e); polish_cards.py scores its start with final_score and records failed included curves (8302a9d); metrics.device_rrms_new now returns NaN for a device with a non-finite or missing included curve and the pipeline's NGSpice validation sorts such candidates last (a0e1e97). Result files written before the fix keep their stored values; out/research/audit/failed_curves.json recomputes the three values for 227 runs, 16 of which have a failed device.

Claim cryo-rounds · updated 2026-10-17

verifiedThe uniform NGSpice FD polish lowers measured-data all-device RRMS by 0.12–0.46 for the inverse models and by 0.0005–0.0582 for the search pipelines; the largest search-pipeline change is pipeline 43 round 1 on the corrected cards (0.2382 → 0.1800).0.6857 → 0.2270 all-device, tandem A round 4, before → after FD; pipeline 7 r4 0.1697 → 0.1643; pipeline 43 r1 / r4, corrected cards, 0.2382 → 0.1800 / 0.1522 → 0.1477

What it is

FD polish: bounded TRF on frozen-inclusion per-curve NGSpice residuals against the target curves, about 400 simulations per device (max_nfev 400, diff_step 0.01, irls 2), in the method's own search box (pooled B: the union of the round 1–4 boxes). Applied identically to every method, on real and the three simulated sets.

Before this study, ngspice_fit.polish used SciPy's relative diff_step/xtol; a start at the box centre (local = 0) stopped after one rejected step. It now uses an absolute-step local Jacobian (xtol = ftol = gtol = 1e-10). Direct NGSpice runs were not affected.

What we did

  • scripts/research/polish_cards.py for every method (queue jobs fdU_* and fd_*), 2026-10-15 17:30 to 2026-10-16 06:42.
  • fd_pipe43_r1_fixed (32 s) and fd_pipe43_r4_fixed (33 s): scripts/research/polish_cards.py (max_nfev 400, diff_step 0.01, irls 2) on the corrected cards out/research/pipe_fixed/full_r1 and full_r4, 2026-10-17 07:12–07:13.

Claim cryo-fd · updated 2026-10-17

verifiedOn the simulated 77–300 K benchmark all three methods reach held-out-temperature RRMS of 0.0004–0.0117 after FD, while the temperature exponents g stay weakly identified.0.0004 / 0.0007 / 0.0117 held-out all-device after FD: NGSpice search / paper-MLP surrogate search / direct NGSpice

What it is

Only 77 K measurements exist, so temperature methods are scored on simulated devices. The released 77 K card (tnom = -196.15 C) cannot be heated (about 0.8 A at 150 K; NGSpice hangs at 300 K); with tnom = 27 C all 18 devices simulate from 77 to 300 K.

p(T) = p_stock * m ** (w(T) ** g),   w = (27 C - T) / 223.15 K, clipped at 0
p(77 K) = p_stock * m;  p(300.15 K) = p_stock

Source src/cryoml/temperature.py

14 numbers per device: log m and log g for the seven paper parameters; BSIM4's own temperature coefficients stay zero. 77 K multipliers anchored on the cold seven-parameter round-4 box. Bank: 10k LHC per device in 1.5× that box with g ∈ [1/4, 4], each simulated at 7 temperatures. Truths: 3 sets × 18 devices in 0.75× with g ∈ [1/3, 3]. Observed 77, 150, 225, 300 K; held out 110, 190, 260 K.

What we did

  • temp_bank_v1 (scripts/research/temp_bank.py, 3,049 s), temp_direct (1,025 s), temp_ngspice_search (1,434 s), temp_sur_paper_mlp (3,099 s), 2026-10-16. All seven temperatures run in one NGSpice process (option temp= re-evaluates temper expressions; identical to separate decks).

Caveats and open checks

  • The truths come from the same card family as the fits (well-specified), and every method reaches ≤0.0117 held-out after FD; this tier does not separate methods. A misspecified tier is the next step for this benchmark.
  • Parameter error stays 0.16–0.27 (local RMS) at RRMS 1e-4, so the g exponents are weakly identifiable from these curves.
  • BSIM4's temperature laws are not built for the cryogenic range; intermediate temperatures are model predictions until measurements at another temperature exist. The 77 K fits move nfactor ×26 from stock, and BSIM4 has no temperature law for nfactor.

Misspecification tiers (GF180 and IHP)

a · well-specified
The seven fitted parameters drawn uniformly in the device's seven-parameter box; every other card value stock; 27 C; no noise.
b · mildly misspecified
A fresh in-box draw, plus every non-fitted misspecification parameter scaled by a log-uniform factor in [1/(1+w), 1+w] (w = 0.2 GF180, 0.05 IHP); extrinsic drain and source resistors outside the card (GF180 r ~ U(25, 100) ohm·µm / W; IHP r = k × RSW1, k ~ U(0.1, 0.4)); multiplicative Gaussian noise σ = 0.01.
c · strongly misspecified
A fresh in-box draw, plus non-fitted parameters with width 0.5; extrinsic resistors r = k × the card's own per-side series resistance, k ~ U(1, 2); self-heating-like heating, curve i at 27 C + ΔT_max · P_i / max P with ΔT_max ~ U(20, 40) K; bias-dependent noise σ(1 + |Vd|/VDD) with σ = 0.01; per-curve gain error 1 + N(0, 0.01).

Refit floors for these tiers: see the floors claim.

Source scripts/research/pdk2/make_truth.py

Scoring

  • SkyWater problems: the paper RRMS (port of the upstream rrmsCalc.py) with the published-baseline curve inclusion frozen; both all-device and combined conventions.
  • GF180 and IHP: the same RRMS with a 1e-10 A trim floor and curve inclusion frozen per target.
  • Budgets and the DEV/TEST split follow the ICML evaluation protocol.

Ilik, L. Mastrodomenico, M. Babaie, F. Sebastiano, TU Delft); main.zip: repository_for_upload_slim/measurement_automation/main/results/dc/*.npy (1,717 files; I3-1 download, 16.3 MB on disk); local copy not committed; read by cryoml.explore.i6_1_tudelft.read_npy_dict (unpickler restricted to numpy reconstruction globals) under python -I.
  • Selection: campaign 1, 69 low-Vt core devices (NF = 1) with a campaign-1 file at both file temperatures; nMOS on die 3, pMOS on die 5; 'array' is the dataset's sub-block (LC low-current, HC high-current). Stage temperature (mean of the file's start and end readings): label 4 = 4.13-4.14 K, label 295 = 295.00-295.01 K; deck temperature = stage temperature of the file.
  • Curves per device and temperature: 12 Id-Vg (idvg@d0..d11; Vd 0.05 V and 11 values to 1.1 V) and 11 Id-Vd (idvd@g0..g10; Vd 0-1.1 V), 111 points each. Vg sweep start: nMOS 0.45 V (4.13 K), 0.3 V (295 K); pMOS -0.6 V, -0.4 V. No deep subthreshold data.
  • Inclusion frozen from the measured current only (pdk2 rule): trim the leading points up to the first |I| > 1e-10 A; include iff the trimmed mean |I| > 3e-7 A (Id-Vd) or > 2e-7 A (Id-Vg). 3161 of 3174 curves included, 22-23 per device and temperature.
  • Float64 currents; smallest nonzero |Id| 4.87e-14 A; no exact zeros; 308 points near Vd = 0 with sign opposite to the bias; no compliance stored; largest |Id| 0.873 mA; no curve repeats its maximum.
  • Split out/research/explore/I6_1/split.json (seed 20261020, by W/L pair; written before any fit): TEST = W/L 4/4 (both polarities) and nMOS 1/0.36, 24 devices; DEV 45 devices in 7 groups. TEST curves are not loaded or simulated by any I6-1 mode. Stock card RRMS: DEV only (no fit), from out/research/explore/I6_1/stock/stock_rrms.json.

  • Card out/research/explore/I6_1/card/ngspice41_ro_17_4_cmosedu50nm_bsim4.mod: BSIM4 level 54 version 4.5.0, N1 (nMOS) and P1 (pMOS) copied verbatim from ngspice-41 examples/mos/ro_17_4.cir ('Short channel models from CMOS Circuit Design, Layout, and Simulation, 50nm BSIM4 models VDD=1V', CMOSedu.com, R. J. Baker); ngspice Modified BSD license. Not a card of the measured 40-nm process. lint 12 nm, no xl (Leff 16 nm at L = 40 nm), toxe 1.4 nm, TNOM 27 C.
  • Temperature: deck .options temp = stage temperature; kt1, kt1l, kt2, ute, ua1, ub1, uc1, at, prt set to 0, so the card values apply at the deck temperature and temperature enters only through the built-in kT/q, band-gap and intrinsic-carrier terms. One card is fitted per device and temperature. BSIM4 is not designed for 4.2 K.
  • Box (cryoml.explore.i6_1_tudelft.base_box, the same for the starting fit and every held-out refit): VTH0, VFB stock +/- 0.5 V, VOFF +/- 0.3 V; other nonzero values log |v|/10..10|v|; zero values: B0, B1 [0, 1e-7] m, CIT, CDSCD [0, 2.5e-3] F/m^2, else inactive. UB has a box but is inactive under the ParameterBox rule (as in the sky130 43-set fits). Active: nMOS 36, pMOS 37 (PRWG is zero in N1).
  • B1 (wider set): universe of 54 BSIM4 names after amendment out/research/explore/I6_1/prereg_amendment_2026-10-20.json (arms.B1 universe: 54 names: DVT0W is removed); edge screen per temperature kept 16 names at 4.13 K and 16 at 295.0 K, the same set: a1, cdsc, dvtp0, dvtp1, fprout, minv, pdiblc1, pdits, pditsd, pditsl, phin, pscbe1, pscbe2, pvag, rdswmin, voffl. Amendment 2: each ngspice process is stopped after 10 s (cryoml.explore.i6_1_tudelft.TIMEOUT_S.
  • Simulator: ngspice-41 native arm64 build, one process per device and card, 23 sweeps on the measured grid, 0.03 s per run. 'at a bound' counts DEV starting cards (45 per temperature, both polarities) with the parameter at a box edge after the starting fit.

  • At 4.13 K R1 is not met (CI upper 1.004); R2 and R3 are met; B1 is beaten, B2 and B3_d3 are not. At 295.0 K R1, R2, R3 are met and every baseline is beaten, which is the opposite of the 295 K prediction.
  • GMR(A, B) = exp(mean ln(RRMS_A / RRMS_B)) over the 45 DEV devices; device bootstrap 10000 resamples, default_rng(0); cluster bootstrap resamples the 7 (polarity, W, L) groups (reported, not deciding; the 2-8 copies of one geometry are not independent). wins = devices with A < B. Recomputed here and checked against out/research/explore/I6_1/decision.json.

  • The outcome list is evaluated in the pre-registered order and the first label whose condition holds is the rule output (scripts/research/explore/i6_1_tudelft.py, function outcome). Each condition is also evaluated on its own here. Rule output: refuted (4.2 K R1 fails: the correction does not lower held-out error where the compact model is used far outside its validity range).
  • Pre-registered interpretation of 'refuted': the correction does not lower held-out error even where BSIM4 is used outside its validity range; together with I5-1 the I3-2 gain is not explained by model-form error of this kind.
  • At 295.0 K the correction lowers the held-out RRMS (R1 met). K > 1 means the M_bias / C0_refit ratio is larger at 4.13 K than at 295.0 K, so the correction lowers the error more at 295.0 K.

  • Per temperature, leave-one-geometry-out over the 7 DEV groups: corrections are trained on the DEV devices of the other 6 groups (both polarities, one network, VDD 1.1 V); every device of the held-out group is refit from its starting card on the 43-parameter box (max_nfev 400, irls 2, diff_step 0.01) and scored on a fresh ngspice-41 simulation of the refit card, multiplied by exp(g) for M_bias, T1_inloop, B3_d3 and B5.
  • all-device = mean over 45 devices (29 nMOS, 16 pMOS); combined = mean of the nMOS and pMOS family means. start = the starting card without a held-out refit. 0 failed devices and 0 simulator timeouts in every arm.
  • B1: base box plus the 16 screened extras (max_nfev 540-550). The B1 refit returned the starting card unchanged (no accepted step) for 16/45 devices at 4.13 K and 13/45 at 295.0 K; B1 is above C0_refit on 34/45 and 33/45 devices.
  • B2: fitted R_ext / box upper median 8.2e-06 (4.13 K) and 9.9e-06 (295.0 K), maximum 0.070 / 0.051; kappa range [-0.099, +0.047] / [-0.018, +0.073].
  • B5 is trained on the held-out device's own measured curves and is an in-sample reference, not a held-out method. Queue jobs I6_1_lodo_4 (1201 s; training 419 s, 315 refits 781 s) and I6_1_lodo_295 (1185 s), 2026-10-20.

  • fraction of mean gap = (C0_refit - M_bias) / (C0_refit - B5); fraction of log GMR = ln GMR(M_bias, C0_refit) / ln GMR(B5, C0_refit). B5 is the in-sample reference (correction trained on the held-out device), so the gap is the part of the C0_refit error that a bias-only correction of this form removes when it sees the device.
  • K = exp(mean_i [ln(M4_i / C4_i) - ln(M295_i / C295_i)]) over the 45 DEV devices (pre-registered temperature contrast); the K row lists the device CI, then the cluster CI. K > 1: the M_bias / C0_refit ratio is larger at 4.13 K.

  • Sources: sky130 out/research/explore/I4_1/real_dev/results.json (12 REAL_DEV devices, 5 nMOS + 7 pMOS; inclusion frozen from the published-card baseline); IHP out/research/explore/I5_1/lodo_233K/results.json, out/research/explore/I5_1/lodo_300K/results.json, out/research/explore/I5_1/lodo_343K/results.json, out/research/explore/I5_1/lodo_398K/results.json, out/research/explore/I5_1/decision.json (18 DEV DUTs; inclusion frozen from the measured current); TU Delft out/research/explore/I6_1/lodo_4K/results.json, out/research/explore/I6_1/lodo_295K/results.json (45 DEV devices in 7 groups; inclusion frozen from the measured current).
  • Same M_bias recipe (I3-2, unchanged) and held-out refit settings (max_nfev 400, irls 2) in every row. Folds: sky130 leave-one-device-out; IHP leave-one-DUT-out within class (LV / HV); TU Delft leave-one-geometry-out (both polarities in one training pool).
  • Card calibration: sky130 77 K uses the paper's 77 K card (parameters published for that temperature) as the refit start; IHP uses the foundry PSP103 card, which the PDK supports at 233-398 K; TU Delft uses a generic 50-nm example card that is not a card of the measured process, with the temperature coefficients set to 0, at 4.13 K and 295.0 K. Every row refits the card per device before scoring.
  • best baseline = lowest all-device mean of B1, B2, B3_d3 (the baselines common to I4-1, I5-1 and I6-1). sky130 also has B3_d2 0.1034 and B4 0.1317, both above B3_d3. B1 and B2 differ between datasets (sky130 B1 19 screened BSIM4 extras, IHP 70-73 PSP extras, TU Delft 16 BSIM4 extras).
  • cluster CI: TU Delft resamples the 7 geometry groups; sky130 and IHP have one device per geometry, so the device bootstrap is the cluster bootstrap there ('= device CI'). fraction of mean gap = (C0_refit - M_bias) / (C0_refit - B5); fraction of log GMR = ln GMR(M_bias, C0_refit) / ln GMR(B5, C0_refit); negative: M_bias above C0_refit.

  • Source: github.com/IHP-GmbH/IHP-Open-PDK ihp-sg13g2/libs.doc/meas/MOS, commit 5e6d592e (Apache-2.0, Keysight IC-CAP MDM text); local copy not committed; parsed as text by cryoml.explore.i5_1_ihp_real.parse_mdm under python -I. 28 DUTs (LV 8 nMOS + 8 pMOS on the same 8 W/L, HV 6 nMOS + 6 pMOS), one DUT per geometry and type, 233/300/343/398 K (header TEMP -40/27/70/125 C).
  • Fitted curves per DUT and temperature: the 11 Vb = 0 curves, Id-Vg at 3 Vd (idvg@d0..d2), Id-Vd at 5 Vg (dc_idvd, idvd@g0..g4) and at 3 near-threshold Vg (dc_idvd_vth, idvd@t0..t2). Body-bias curves are stored and not used. The dc_idvd / dc_idvd_vth gate biases are set per DUT and temperature by the measurement setup.
  • Inclusion is frozen from the measured current only (pdk2 rule): trim the leading points up to the first |I| > 1e-10 A; include iff the trimmed mean |I| > 3e-7 A (Id-Vd) or > 2e-7 A (Id-Vg). 946 of 1232 curves included; 3 to 10 per DUT and temperature.
  • Up to 6 significant digits; smallest nonzero |Id| 2e-14 A; largest |Id| is 0.061 of the 0.1 A drain compliance; off-current floor 2e-14 to 6.3e-12 A (median 1.3e-13 A).
  • Split out/research/explore/I5_1/split.json (seed 20261020): LV by geometry (3 of 8 geometries, both polarities, to TEST), HV 2 of 6 per polarity to TEST; DEV 18 (LV 10, HV 8), TEST 10. Written before any fit; the fitting modes read only DEV. Stock card RRMS: NGSpice-46 + psp103.osdi, stock PDK card, no fit.

  • Pre-registration out/research/explore/I5_1/prereg.json (commit 9267a90, committed before any card fit). Decision at 300 K over the 18 DEV DUTs: 'replicated' if R1 (CI upper bound of GMR(M_bias, C0_refit) < 1), R2 (M_bias all-device mean <= T1_inloop mean + 0.005) and R3 (0 failed M_bias DUTs) all hold. Baselines B1, B2, B3_d3: X is beaten if the CI upper bound of GMR(M_bias, X) < 1; 'supported against baselines' if replicated and every X is beaten, otherwise 'matched by' the X not beaten.
  • Rule output at 300 K: not replicated (R1 fails); baseline rule output: matched by B1, B2. 233, 343 and 398 K are secondary (reported, not deciding); R1 fails at each of them.
  • GMR(A, B) = exp(mean ln(RRMS_A / RRMS_B)) over the 18 DEV DUTs; device bootstrap, 10000 resamples, default_rng(0); wins = DUTs with A < B. Recomputed here from the stored per-DUT values and checked against out/research/explore/I5_1/decision.json.
  • DEV values are development evidence (the rule, budgets, box and arms were fixed after the stock-card RRMS was seen and before any fit). TEST (10 DUTs) is not loaded by any I5-1 fitting mode.

  • Per temperature, leave-one-DUT-out over the 18 DEV DUTs (9 nMOS, 9 pMOS), corrections trained within class (LV: 9 training DUTs, HV: 7), VDD 1.2 V (LV) / 3.3 V (HV). Every held-out arm refits the held-out DUT's card from its starting card on the 12-parameter box (max_nfev 400, irls 2, diff_step 0.01) and scores a fresh NGSpice-46 simulation of the refit card, multiplied by exp(g) for M_bias, T1_inloop, B3_d3 and B5.
  • all-device = mean over 18 DUTs; nMOS and pMOS family means have 9 DUTs each, so combined = all-device. start = the starting card without a held-out refit.
  • B1 extras from the edge screen (out/research/explore/I5_1/start/b1_screen.json; response >= 1e-4 at a box edge on a 300 K starting card of the class): LV 75 and HV 76 of 92 PSP candidates; 70-73 active per DUT (nonzero stock value). B1 and B2 max_nfev scaled with the parameter count (same TRF evaluations per IRLS round as the base box). B2 at 300 K: fitted R_ext / box upper median 0.0019 [4.9e-10, 0.101], kappa median -0.0006.
  • B5 is trained on the held-out DUT's own measured curves and is an in-sample reference, not a held-out method. Queue jobs I5_1_lodo_300 (07:59-08:07), _233 (08:07-08:15), _343 (08:15-08:23), _398 (08:23-08:30), 2026-10-20; 126 held-out refits per temperature, about 472 s each.

The truths also contain an extrinsic resistance per side k * R_side_stock / W, k ~ U(1, 2), which has the B2 form, and a per-curve temperature rise (27 C + dT_max * P_i / max P, dT_max ~ U(20, 40) K); the B2 heating term is pointwise and multiplicative, not the truth's per-curve temperature.

  • B5 (pre-registered, not in the rule): M_bias-form ensemble (3-16-16-1, 5 seeds) g0 trained on the held-out device's own starting-card record; held-out card refit with g0 in the loop; g1 = same recipe trained on the refit card's record; score = refit card x exp(g1). B5 uses the held-out device's measured curves to train g and is an in-sample bound for a bias-only correction of this form, not a held-out method.
  • fraction of mean gap = (C0_refit - M_bias) / (C0_refit - B5) on all-device (REAL_DEV) or all-target (GF180/IHP) means; fraction of log GMR = ln GMR(M_bias, C0_refit) / ln GMR(B5, C0_refit).
  • M_bias is above B5 on every device and target (0 wins on all three datasets).

I3-2 caveats and open checks
itemdetail
REAL_DEV reuseREAL_DEV was used for the design and the decision of E1 and I2-1, and the I3-2 hypothesis was formed from the REAL_DEV T1 and M results. The I3-2 REAL_DEV values are development evidence, not a held-out test.
Input choice after I2-1The 3-input set (no geometry, no simulated current) was chosen after the E1 and I2-1 REAL_DEV results were seen. The pre-registration fixed it before any M_bias result existed, but the choice is not independent of REAL_DEV.
M_bias vs T1_inloopM_bias / T1_inloop R = 0.968 [0.920, 1.011], 7/12 devices lower; the CI includes 1. R2 tests M_bias <= T1 + 0.005 (non-inferiority), not M_bias < T1.
Verilog-A not compiledm_bias_sky130_dev_full.va (full 12-device model, 207 lines) is text only; the emitted assignments were evaluated in Python on 200 random bias points (maxg difference1.6e-11). It has not been compiled (OpenVAF / ngspice OSDI) or simulated. abs() folds reverse-mode bias onto forward mode; reverse bias does not occur in any record.
REAL_TEST untouchedNo I3_2 script loads the 6 REAL_TEST devices. A REAL_TEST evaluation happens only at the method freeze, with the configuration fixed before it is loaded.
12 devices5 nMOS and 7 pMOS; the bootstrap resamples 12 devices. pmos_L0p35_W0p55 contributes 36% of the M_bias all-device sum (RRMS 0.3496); without it the M_bias mean is 0.0561 vs C0_refit 0.0798 (diagnostic only).
Held-out refit uses measured dataThe held-out card refit (box 6 of the process diagram) fits the held-out device's 43 parameters to its measured curves, as card extraction does. Only g is held out. C0_refit uses the same refit without g.
Simulated R4 marginR4 needs R <= 0.90 on one PDK. GF180: R = 0.880 [0.837, 0.921], T1_inloop lower than M_bias (R(M_bias, T1_inloop) = 1.023 [0.982, 1.066]). IHP: R = 0.885 [0.789, 1.005] (the CI includes 1); R(M_bias, T1_inloop) = 0.950 [0.874, 1.036]. Simulated devices with injected misspecification; secondary to REAL_DEV.
Figures from stored dataThe g surface is the in-sample full model. The I-V figures show the starting card and starting card x exp(g); the refit-card curves are not stored and were not re-simulated.

  • Stage 1 (post-hoc): each arm is trained on 11 devices and applied once to the held-out device's fixed best 43-parameter card (direct NGSpice round 3 + FD). C0 = that card with no correction.
  • Stage 2 (refit): the held-out card is re-polished (ngspice_fit.polish, TRF max_nfev 400, irls 2, diff_step 0.01, round-3 box) against the measured curves with the fold's correction inside the residual. C0 = the same polish without correction from the same start; T1 is re-polished with T1 in the loop.
  • Pre-registered continue rule (all five): M all-device <= 0.090; M < T1 all-device; M < T1 on >= 8/12; M < C0 on >= 8/12; 0 failed devices for M. Stage 1: no, no, no, no, yes. Stage 2: yes, no, no, yes, yes.
  • all-device = mean over the 12 REAL_DEV devices (5 nMOS, 7 pMOS); combined = mean of the nMOS and pMOS family means. T1 is a table indexed by curve tag and is not a function of terminal voltages, so it cannot be written as a Verilog-A device model; M can.

NGSpice in place of the surrogate———————18/180.11250.10530.04100.169600
  • Script: scripts/research/surrogate_arch_study.py on out/cold_loop/full/round_1 (cache) and data/processed/cold_loop/full_r1 (bank), seed 20260818. The training subset at fraction f is the first round(f × 85,853) indices of one fixed permutation of the pipeline's training split; validation and test splits are unchanged.
  • Fractions 1/8, 1/4, 1/2: queue job archlc_full_r1 (first attempt 2026-10-18 03:38, killed rc=143 after 10,138 s; restarted 2026-10-19 09:01, finished 10:05; the restart skipped finished reports and trained fno_f0.5). Fraction 1: the reports of arch_full_r1 (2026-10-16/17), same script, split and seed.
  • Recipe: AdamW lr 1e-3, weight decay 1e-5, cosine schedule, batch 512, early stopping (patience 25) on validation loss; at most 200 epochs (FNO 80).
  • End-to-end = fps.finite_difference_surrogate_extract with the trained surrogate frozen: 8 starts, TRF max_nfev 100, diff_step 0.02, regularization 1e-4, NGSpice validation of the top 4 endpoints, the first 4 starts and the published fallback; the selected card is re-simulated in NGSpice on the measured 77 K data. One fixed method per row; no per-device selection across rows.
  • all-device = mean over 18 devices; combined = mean of the nMOS (8) and pMOS (10) family means. bank start = devices whose selected card is one of the LHC bank starts (selected_candidate_kind lhc_start) rather than an FD endpoint; bank starts are the same for every surrogate, so rows with many bank-start selections share per-device values.
  • The end-to-end search ran on the 18 measured devices; it is a diagnostic ablation and is not used for method selection.

  • Training: every architecture uses the same cache (out/cold_loop/full/round_1/cache), the same per-device train/validation/test split as the pipeline (seed 20260818; 85,853 training samples), the same loss (standardized signed-log MSE + curve-normalized linear Huber) and the same recipe (AdamW, cosine schedule, early stopping on validation loss, at most 200 epochs; FNO at most 80). time (s) = training wall time.
  • loss = the pipeline's forward loss on the held-out bank samples. curve NRMSE = per held-out sample, mean over the 11 curves of RMSE / max|I| of the simulated curve (floor 1e-3 of the sample's largest curve); an emulator diagnostic, not the paper RRMS. The mean curve NRMSE is 2.8e+04 to 2.8e+06 times the median.
  • |score err.| = mean over 18 devices and 3 reference cards (stored pipeline r1 pick, direct NGSpice cold, direct NGSpice seeded) of |surrogate-predicted RRMS − NGSpice RRMS|. direct fit ranked better = devices where the direct NGSpice cold card (out/research/ngspice_direct/full_r1_direct_cold) has a lower RRMS than the stored pipeline r1 pick, by the surrogate's prediction and by NGSpice. The stored pipeline r1 picks were made before the failed-curve fix; the pick for nmos_L0p15_W1p6 has 1 of 10 included curves failed, and its NGSpice reference value 0.2035 averages the surviving curves.
  • End-to-end = the pipeline's search (fps.finite_difference_surrogate_extract) with the trained surrogate frozen: 8 starts, TRF max_nfev 100, diff_step 0.02, regularization 0.0001, NGSpice validation of the top 4 endpoints, the first 4 starts and the published fallback; RRMS of the selected card re-simulated in NGSpice on the measured 77 K data. start picked = devices whose selected card is one of the bank starts (selected_candidate_kind lhc_start) rather than an FD endpoint. all-device = mean over 18 devices; combined = mean of the nMOS (8) and pMOS (10) family means.
  • Reference rows: NGSpice in place of the surrogate = the same search code with NGSpice as the evaluator (out/research/swap_search/full_round_1). pipeline r1, stored = the cold-loop round-1 extraction (out/cold_loop/full/round_1/extract). pipeline r1, corrected = its final selection rerun with the same surrogate and failed-curve rejection (out/research/pipe_fixed/full_r1). The pipeline rows' training columns are the cold-loop round-1 forward model (same split and seed, 10,730 test samples); its ranking counts come from out/research/surrogate_gap_full_round_1.json and the pipe_fixed records.
  • End-to-end records of the architecture study store rrms without per_curve. The run started 2026-10-16 22:26 (out/research/done.txt), after commit a0e1e97 (21:52), with which metrics.device_rrms_new returns NaN for a device whose frozen-inclusion curve is non-finite or missing and the pipeline's NGSpice validation sorts such candidates last. A finite stored rrms is therefore counted as a valid device and a non-finite one as failed.
  • Reference: pipeline r1, stored (method output): 1 failed device(s): nmos_L0p15_W1p6 (1 included curve(s) non-finite); valid-only all-device 0.2395 over 17 devices, combined 0.2238; penalized all-device 0.2920.
  • The end-to-end search in this study ran on the 18 measured devices; it was queued before the DEV/TEST protocol was fixed. It is reported as a diagnostic ablation and is not used for method selection.

decided Which toolchain runs the IHP SG13G2 PSP 103.6 model?

The prebuilt macOS OpenVAF-Reloaded build compiles the OSDI model; it runs on Homebrew ngspice-46, isolated from the ngspice-41 configuration.

Recorded 2026-10-16

Source src/cryoml/pdk2/__init__.py

decided Cap u0 below the BSIM4 u0 > 1 unit switch?

No. The u0 range of the cold boxes stays unchanged.

BSIM4 divides u0 by 1e4 when u0 > 1; the cold round-1 box (u0 ×100) crosses that value for about 14% of nMOS samples. The trust-region arms use a 1e-3 Jacobian step and a cliff guard.
